plan.thesis: After this pass TestPilot is a single-user, loopback-only tool for running and tracking automated tests across the 10 product surfaces: PushEngage (marketing site, app dashboard, WP plugin, Shopify app, Android SDK, iOS SDK) and LedgerPort (marketing site, SaaS dashboard, WP plugin, Shopify app). The nav drops from 22 visible items to 5. (1) Products, at '/'. One card per surface, driven by the server framework registry. Each card shows the last honest verdict, the session state with a copyable capture command, the latest master commit and the CI conclusion, and has one Run control: Smoke, Full, one spec, one npm script, or a Maestro/iOS flow. The shared RunPanel sits below. (2) Test Cases. The ~2.5k imported Playwright cases plus the mobile and manual cases; run one, a selection, or on a device; each history row links to its Run Story. (3) Runs. Run history and the Run Story evidence view. (4) Schedules & CI. Local monitors that stay awake and notify on failure, plus read-only GitHub Actions status per product. (5) Settings, with three tabs: Sessions, Fixtures, and Data (TM backups and restore). The parts that make results trustworthy stay and get hardened: the runner, the V1 verdict floor, the I1 session gate and canary, the scheduler, the G3 guards, and the SQLite TM store, which gets conflict-safe writes. The rest is deleted, not hidden: the simulated cockpit and its mock data; the Asana/GitHub/Slack task queue and its write-backs; all in-app AI; SKB Docs; the TestCollab Plans/Runs/Requirements/Traceability/Releases/Defects/Risks modules; Performance; local Pipelines; Manual Test; Asana intake; the 10 seed source files; and, if you confirm, login/users/hosting. That is about 20k of the ~34.5k src+server lines, about 35% of the 1.07 MB bundle, and about 12 npm packages. CI becomes real through one matrix workflow that runs each framework's own scripts, applies the same verdict floor, uploads artifacts and is linked from TestPilot. Auth-gated and mobile suites stay on the local runner behind the session gate. Because the root repo (KulvinderGosal/QAAutomations) is PUBLIC and most framework folders are not committed, the CI change is delivered as a reviewed local branch and is never pushed automatically.

refine.name: R2 · Safety net: contract tests for kept external routes + typecheck the server
refine.what: Add `npm run test:contract` (node:test via tsx, the same pattern as test:verdict). It mounts mountAll on an ephemeral port with a stubbed runner and scheduler, and asserts status and response shape for every route an outside caller uses: GET /api/runner/frameworks; POST /api/runner/runs with Origin → {run:{id,status}}; GET /api/runner/runs/:id?offset → status, verdict{state,cls,counts,reason,humanAction}, output; GET /api/runner/scripts; GET /api/reports/history → history[].id/verdict; GET /api/sessions[?cached=1]; /api/schedule list|create|:id/run|:id/toggle|alert-status|test-alert; GET /api/tm/state and POST /api/tm/save {state,reason}. refine.name: R3 · Target information architecture: 5 nav items, one run surface
refine.what: NAV (Sidebar.tsx, 22 visible items → 5): Products `/` · Test Cases `/tests` · Runs `/runs` (+ `/runs/:id`) · Schedules & CI `/schedule` · Settings `/settings`. A catch-all `*` route goes to `/`. HEADER: brand toggle (PushEngage / LedgerPort / All), honoured by all four content screens; SessionBadge; theme toggle; TM 'DB offline' banner (R5). No bell, no global search. (1) PRODUCTS replaces TM Dashboard, Overview, Test Runner and the Pipelines cards. It shows 10 cards from /api/runner/frameworks (R4): PE marketing site, PE app dashboard, PE WP plugin, PE Shopify, PE Android SDK (iam-android, maestro), PE iOS SDK (iam-ios, ios-sim), LP marketing site, LP SaaS, LP WP plugin, LP Shopify. Each card shows the last local verdict (state + reason + humanAction via verdictNote), a CI chip (R6) linking to the GitHub run, a persona chip (ok/warn/block + Copy capture cmd), the next scheduled fire, and the latest master commit (read-only). Each card has ONE Run control: mode Smoke | Full | Spec… (spec picker from /api/runner/specs) | Script… (npm scripts from /api/runner/scripts, i.e. command mode) | Flow… (mobile), plus env and headed. A top banner reads 'N sessions need you' with their capture commands. The single shared RunPanel is docked at the bottom. (2) TEST CASES: the existing suite tree and case list. The default filter is Automated, with a toggle for All. It keeps select-all, Run selected (sequential), Stop, staging/production env with a production confirm (R8), Run on device, Import from frameworks (refresh, marks stale, never deletes), and suite add/rename/clone/move/delete. The case modal shows steps, verdict notes and history rows linking to /runs/:id. It adds a status-count strip and the docked RunPanel. Removed: Copilot, Asana import, comments/review, plan and requirement fields, the DeviceRunReports modal. (3) RUNS: the history table from /api/reports/history (filter by product, verdict and source: manual/scheduled/case), with rows linking to Run Story. It replaces Reports and QA Log. (4) SCHEDULES & CI: local jobs (list/create/toggle/run-now/delete, last verdict, session-blocked state) plus the read-only CI panel per product (R6). It replaces Pipelines and the Scheduler terminal. (5) SETTINGS has three tabs. Sessions is the Test sessions panel moved from TestRunner.tsx (per-persona state, Re-probe, Verify live, Copy capture cmd). Fixtures is the read-only registry view moved from /fixtures; the Integrations test-store bookmarks derive from it. Data lists TM backups with restore (R10) and export. Retire the routes /overview, /queue, /queue/:id, /runner, /pipelines, /manual, /qa-log, /fixtures, /reports, /skb-docs, /integrations, /users, /database and all /tests/* subroutes.
refine.why: The user asked for a stupid-simple tool with roughly 4-6 menus. Today 10 UIs start real runs (TestRunner, TestPlans RunAutomation, TaskRunnerCard, Pipelines, the Scheduler terminal and run-now, the Reports builder and Re-run 5×, ManualTest, TestCases, TestRuns, QaQueue), plus 6 simulated 'run' buttons. The brand toggle shows everywhere but only 6 screens read it. Collapsing to one run control per product, and one case-run path in Test Cases, covers every real run in the 200-run history.

Derive the Products cards, the brand filter and the TM suite↔framework binding from that response. Delete the client copies: TM_FRAMEWORKS (src/tm/types.ts:341, 8 of 11 entries, missing the mobile ones), FRAMEWORK_PRODUCT (src/tm/store.ts ~57), PRODUCT_FRAMEWORK (src/lib/qaPlanner.ts:35, with the lp-shopify→ledgerport-saas-automation bug at :43) and the mock product catalog (src/data/mock.ts:70-178, fake coverage %). refine.name: R5 · TM write integrity: no silent overwrites of the shared DB
refine.what: (1) Add a monotonic `rev` to tm_state. GET /api/tm/state returns it; POST /api/tm/save requires `baseRev` and returns 409 {rev} on a mismatch; the client re-hydrates and re-applies its single mutation. Scripted saves pass the baseRev from their own GET; for one-off bulk edits, `force:true` with a reason starting 'script:'/'prune:'. (2) Delete the case-count reconcile at src/tm/store.ts:1271 and its 'hydrate-reconcile' push. (3) When hydrate can't reach the server (store.ts:1252-1253), go read-only and show the Header 'DB offline, changes not saved' banner; don't arm pushToServer (store.ts:925) on a stale mirror. (4) Drop the full 2.4 MB localStorage mirror: it sits near the ~5 MB quota and save() swallows QuotaExceededError. (5) Coalesce mutations into one debounced save, and in bulk runs persist once per run, not per case. (6) Turn the saveState >90%-drop warning (server/tmStore.ts:162) into a refusal unless reason starts with 'prune:'.
refine.why: Every server/*.ts edit restarts the LaunchAgent's Vite (149 restarts logged). Any tab that hydrated before a Claude /api/tm/save, or during a restart, can overwrite the whole DB last-writer-wins. Backup #10 (2908 cases after 2960) shows the reconcile path firing. The DB is the only durable record of results, and useTm.serverDown is set but never shown.

refine.name: R6 · Make CI real: one GitHub Actions matrix + the same verdict floor + a CI view in TestPilot (proposed on a branch, never pushed)
refine.what: PRECONDITION. CI can only run code it can check out. Today pushengage-app-dashboard, ledgerport-saas-automation, ledgerport-shopify and packages/qa-core have 0 tracked files in the root repo; pushengage-site has 1, pushengage-wp-plugin 3, pushengage-shopify-revamped 6. ledgerport-wp-plugin is its own public repo (KulvinderGosal/wordpress-ledgerport-autmation), and the LP marketing framework lives in awesomemotive/pushengage-ledgerport-site (11 test files on master). The frameworks + qa-core must first be committed to the repo chosen in askUser #2, after a secret scan; .env and .auth/ are already gitignored. WORKFLOW `.github/workflows/qa-fleet.yml` (replaces U15). Triggers: `on: schedule` (cron '30 2 * * 0,3' = Sun/Wed 08:00 IST) + `workflow_dispatch` (inputs: framework, script). NO pull_request/pull_request_target, so forks of a public repo never get secrets. `permissions: contents: read`. Job `qa (${{ matrix.id }})` with `strategy: {fail-fast: false, matrix: {include: [...]}}`, `timeout-minutes: 45`, `concurrency: qa-${{ matrix.id }}`. PHASE-1 LEGS are the suites that need no human-captured session: {id: pushengage-site, dir: pushengage-site, script: test:scheduled:prod}, {id: ledgerport-marketing-site, dir: ledgerport-sites/pushengage-ledgerport-site, script: test:scheduled:prod}, {id: ledgerport-saas-automation, dir: ledgerport-saas-automation, script: test:public}. STEPS: actions/checkout and setup-node (Node 22) pinned by SHA, npm cache keyed on `${{ matrix.dir }}/package-lock.json`; then in `working-directory: ${{ matrix.dir }}`: `npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `npm run ${{ matrix.script }} -- --reporter=list,json` with env `CI=1` and `PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=$RUNNER_TEMP/results.json`; per-leg secrets go only in an `env:` block, never echoed and never placed in run arguments or issue bodies. Then `npx tsx TestPilot/scripts/ci-verdict.ts $RUNNER_TEMP/results.json`, a ~40-line wrapper around the pure `deriveVerdict` in server/qaLoop/verdict.ts (it needs qa-core/errors committed). CI then gets the same PASS/PASS_WITH_GAPS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN floor: it writes verdict.json and a $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY table, exits 1 only on FAIL, and on BLOCKED exits 0 with ::warning. Upload artifacts `if: always()`: playwright-report/, results.json, verdict.json, retention-days 14, trace/video off on prod legs, with no GitHub Pages publishing. PHASE 2, only after a local proof: WP-admin legs that log in from secrets without a captcha (ledgerport-wp-plugin is selfHeal from WP_ADMIN_USER/PASS; pushengage-wp-plugin staging), with secrets in a GitHub Environment `qa-staging` that requires a reviewer. STAYS LOCAL: the Shopify, app-dashboard and LP SaaS/Shopify staging legs (their sessions need Turnstile/hCaptcha/passkey/2FA by a human; never upload .auth storageState as a secret) and mobile (Maestro/iOS sim). Those run through the local Scheduler behind the I1 gate. CLOUDFLARE CAVEAT: GitHub-hosted IPs may be challenged on pushengage.com/ledgerport.com. The verdict floor reports that as BLOCKED{ENV}, not FAIL. If it happens, use a self-hosted Mac runner, which is safe only in a PRIVATE repo. TESTPILOT SIDE: Pipelines is replaced, not merged (U7). Add a read-only `GET /api/ci/status` in server/github.ts: GitHub REST `GET /repos/{TP_CI_REPO}/actions/workflows/{TP_CI_WORKFLOW}/runs?per_page=5`, then `/actions/runs/{id}/jobs`; map job name `qa (<id>)` to framework id; return [{framework, conclusion, startedAt, durationSec, htmlUrl}], cached 5 min, needing only GITHUB_TOKEN read access. Render it as the CI panel on Schedules & CI and a chip on each Products card. Phase 1 has no 'Run in CI' button, because workflow_dispatch is a write; it can be added later behind ConfirmDialog + nonce. Once a CI leg is green for 2 consecutive cycles, disable its duplicate local schedule. Deliver the workflow, ci-verdict.ts and the CI view as a local branch plus diff for review.
refine.why: The user asked to keep the CI/CD pipeline in mind. The existing workflows can't pass, two of them leak data in a public repo, and the local Pipelines feature has never run. One matrix that calls each framework's own scripts is the simplest CI that matches how the suites are actually run. Reusing deriveVerdict means CI and TestPilot report the same honest state, and linking runs from TestPilot keeps one place to look.

refine.name: R7 · Make the scheduled monitors an honest, loud signal (and impossible to double-fire)
refine.what: (1) Spawn scheduler-fired runs under `caffeinate -i -w <childPid>` (server/runner.ts, when the source is the scheduler). (2) Stagger the two Sunday 08:00 jobs (LP 08:00, PE site 10:00) in .testpilot-schedules.json. (3) watchRunForAlert (server/scheduler.ts:149-167) currently stops after 720 ticks (~60 min); make it wait for a terminal status. (4) Since Slack is removed, send every scheduled FAIL/BLOCKED verdict through macNotify (scheduler.ts:376), and have /api/schedule/alert-status return {ready:true, channel:'macos'} for the skill. (5) Triage the reds: aggregate failing test titles over the last 10 scheduled runs per framework, and quarantine known-red and staging-only tests out of test:scheduled:prod in pushengage-site and the LP marketing framework (framework-repo edits, reviewed). Add `,json` to their `--reporter` so local and CI verdicts get per-test counts. (6) Take a pid lock (.testpilot-scheduler.lock) in startScheduler, and change .claude/launch.json 'testpilot-dev' (currently `npm run dev`, autoPort:true) to a url-only attach to http://localhost:5173, so an agent can never start a second scheduler beside the LaunchAgent. (7) Retire the launchd smoke-monitor jobs per askUser #3; unloading a LaunchAgent is persistent config and needs the user's explicit OK at implementation time.
refine.why: The Scheduler is the only heavily used feature, yet 45 of 46 scheduled runs failed and 0 alerts were delivered (SLACK_BOT_TOKEN empty, 'skipped' ×45). The 10-18 LP run took 307.7 min with ~298 min asleep, and PE site started 5 h late behind it. A permanently red, silent monitor is noise. There are three overlapping schedulers today (TestPilot, smoke-all, smoke-auth-ctas).

refine.name: R10 · Bound DB growth and give backups a restore UI
refine.what: In server/tmStore.ts, replace the count-only MAX_BACKUPS=50 (line 35) with tiered retention: the last 10, plus 1/day for 14 days, plus 1/week for 8 weeks. Store snapshots gzip-compressed (node:zlib), run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) after each write, and run one VACUUM after pruning. Settings→Data lists /api/tm/backups (reason, counts, size) and restores through a ConfirmDialog, using the already-written but never-called listTmBackups/restoreTmBackup (src/lib/tmStore.ts). Require X-TP-Nonce on POST /api/tm/restore, which replaces the whole state.
refine.why: 19 full snapshots take 44.4 MB of the 49.3 MB DB (~90%); the live state is 2.4 MB, and at the cap the file reaches ~120 MB. The backup safety net has no UI, and restore is a destructive route guarded only by Origin.

verifies.summary:
Dependency audit of the 18 removal units and 13 refinements. I grepped TestPilot/src, server, vite.config.ts and package.json, ~/.claude/skills (testpilot-qa), ~/QA-Automations/.claude/skills, the framework package.json files and scripts, packages/qa-core, the LaunchAgents and the memory files. Everything was read-only.

Rule used for `safe`:
- safe=false: following the unit as written breaks something outside TestPilot's own `npm run build` gate (qa-core, a framework script, the always-on LaunchAgent, live state), or breaks the build because of a landing order the plan does not state.
- safe=true: the removal itself is sound and only needs the extra touch-points listed. All of those are mechanical, and most are tsc-detectable because noUnusedLocals is on in both tsconfigs.

Load-bearing problems the plan missed:
1. **U8 package.json line.** TestPilot's `@playwright/test` devDep cannot be removed. packages/qa-core/tsconfig.json maps `@playwright/test` and its typeRoots to `../../TestPilot/node_modules`. qa-core/selftest/types.selftest.ts imports a type from it. The plan's "only if grep finds no other importer" check only searches TestPilot, so it would wrongly clear the removal and break `npm run typecheck|check` in qa-core.
2. **`tsx` is cross-repo load-bearing.** These all run `../TestPilot/node_modules/.bin/tsx`: `auth:probe` in 5 frameworks (spawned by the kept I1 session canary and run gate), `auth:capture:human`, `auth:spike-a`, `spike:b-login`, and the qa-core `selftest` plus probe-fixtures.selftest.ts. Moving tsx to devDependencies (U18) is fine. It must never leave TestPilot along with `start` (U12).
3. **Landing order is unstated and breaks both server and client builds:**
   - U4 (skbDocs imports ./aiTest and github.getPullRequest) and U9 (flaky imports ./aiTest) must land before or with U2 and U3.
   - U5 must land before U2's lib/github trim (tm/store.ts:12 imports `GithubPr`; TestPlans uses fetchPr/listPrs) and before U3 (tm/store.ts:1887 createPlanFromPr uses defaultFrameworkFor).
   - U11 must land with or after U2 (asanaHandler's scrubTask uses intake.scrub).
   - R4 must land before U1 and U13 (seed() at tm/store.ts:568 uses mock `products`).
   - R3 must land before U14 (`/` route).
4. **The LaunchAgent com.testpilot.dev runs `npm run dev` from this same TestPilot folder, and 98%+ of TestPilot is untracked.**
   - A "local branch" does not isolate the work.
   - Every server/*.ts edit restarts Vite and kills any in-flight run.
   - A broken intermediate state makes Vite log "server restart failed" (node_modules/vite chunks/node.js:25770) and keep running the old code silently. A reboot in that state leaves TestPilot down, so the Sun/Wed monitors would not fire.
   - Do the prune in a copy and swap it in when green.
5. **R2 contract tests would mutate live state.**
   - tmStore's DB_PATH is hard-coded to ~/QA-Automations/testpilot-tm.db (server/tmStore.ts:33-34).
   - The schedules, sessions and runs files are cwd-relative (scheduler.ts:43, sessions.ts:494, runner.ts:732).
   - GET /api/sessions without `cached=1` spawns real `auth:probe` processes.
   - Tests need a temp cwd and HOME (or a DB-path override) and must use cached=1.
6. **U15 is mis-framed.** Only smoke-tests.yml is tracked and on origin/main, and it has been workflow_dispatch-only since commit 3f1dca0 (2026-02-23). playwright.yml, qa-publish-reports.yml and the two qa-wp-pushengage-*.yml files are untracked local files that were never pushed. They are not live public leak vectors, but deleting them is unrecoverable, so they must go into the R1 archive.

verifies.summary:
Data & Safety verification, read-only (GETs to localhost:5173 and immutable SQLite reads only). The prune is data-safe: every TM collection the plan removes is empty in the live state and in all 19 backups. That covers plans, executions, requirements, risks, releases, defects, perfRuns and deviceRuns, plus 0 externalRef, 0 non-empty requirementIds and 0 comments. Hydration ignores unknown keys, and all seed guards equal their code versions. Removing U2, U4, U6 and U8 deletes every real external write and every user-URL outbound path, which is a safety gain. G3 is untouched: requestGuard is mounted separately from auth, and nonces are checked per handler.

Most important finding: the hydrate-reconcile in src/tm/store.ts:1271 has already reverted user data. On 2026-09-22 at 16:41 the user's 'dedupe-iam-dashboard (final)' removed 52 imp- cases and suite imp-suite-pushengage-app-dashboard-in-app-campaigns (backup 9→10, 2960→2908). The 16:48:58 hydrate-reconcile wrote a stale 2960-case mirror back, and all 52 are in the live DB now. So U13's seedcase prune is unsafe until R5 removes the reconcile and old tabs are reloaded.

Other unsafe items:
- **R2:** the contract tests would hit the hard-coded live DB and the cwd-relative .testpilot-* files. A test-created schedule would later fire against production.
- **R5:** restores of small backups get refused, bulk-run verdicts can be lost, and a failed push during a restart is silently dropped.
- **R6:** a BLOCKED leg exits 0, so the CI chip shows success and can switch off the local monitor. The JSON output path isn't expanded, so the verdict file goes missing. Several untracked dirs are not gitignored (config/fixtures.json, testpilot-qa-records, testpilot-device-reports, HostReady, smoke-reports). Artifacts on a public repo are readable by any signed-in user. CI must never set the prod form/signup switches.
- **R7:** a pid lock would break the scheduler on Vite's in-process restarts, and hand-edits to .testpilot-schedules.json are clobbered. The 08:00 collision is on both Sunday and Wednesday.
- **R8:** stale-marking line-keyed imp- ids strands case history.
- **R10:** gzip would make legacy backups unrestorable, and pruning deletes backup #10, the only deduped snapshot.
- **R1:** the snapshot leaves out run history, Run Story details, schedules and sessions, plus the untracked items being deleted.

Evidence corrections:
- **U15:** 4 of the 5 workflows were never committed (0 commits, untracked), so the claimed public leaks never happened. Deleting them is permanent, so archive them first.
- **U12:** HostReady is an untracked plain dir, not a git repo, and holds a unique SAAS_PLAN.md. Archive it unconditionally.

designs.thesis: After this pass, TestPilot should be a single-user, loopback-only tool with three jobs. These are the only jobs the evidence shows anyone doing. (1) Run the framework suites and TM-bound cases through one runner (Playwright spec/smoke/full/command plus the Maestro and iOS device modes), behind the V1 honest-verdict floor and the I1 session gate. Run Story is the evidence view, and run history keeps serving as the API the testpilot-qa skill depends on. (2) Hold the Test Cases repository (suites, cases, results) in the SQLite DB. Claude sessions write to it safely through a small per-entity API instead of seed .ts files, and the user browses and runs it from one Test Cases screen. (3) Run the twice-weekly prod monitors so that a failure actually reaches a human. Everything else gets deleted, not hidden: the simulated cockpit and its mock data; the QA Queue, Task Detail, Overview and QA Log stack, which gh and the Asana MCP replaced in July; all in-app AI behind the unfunded key; SKB Docs; Pipelines; Manual Test; the seven empty TestCollab modules; Performance; the TM Dashboard; and the login/roles/hosting layer. That takes 27 routes down to about 4 (/tests, /runner with a History tab, /runs/:id, /schedule), removes roughly 17-19k of the ~34.5k lines in src+server, drops 13 npm packages, and cuts about a third of the 1.07 MB bundle (seeds 169 KB, mock 26 KB, react-query 25 KB, unused screens 83 KB+). The kept core is then made trustworthy: no lost TM writes, monitors that stay awake and notify someone, and case runs whose live output and evidence can be seen from the case.

designs.thesis: TestPilot should become the system of record and honest executor for the QA loop as it is actually run. Today that loop is: paste an Asana gid or PR link, test UI-first in Claude-in-Chrome or on a device, use curl or Playwright as the oracle, file to GitHub through report-qa-finding, then verify, gh close and complete in Asana. TestPilot currently sits beside that loop instead of in it. Since 2026-09-01 only 1 of 33 runner runs was interactive, no UI save has ever reached the TM DB (0 'pre:save' backups out of 19), and results were recorded by writing new seed .ts files until 09-27, then not at all. After this pass, TestPilot is five things. (1) The runner plus the V1 verdict floor, the I1 session gate and one scheduler that actually alerts. (2) A test-case ledger that Claude writes to over a small versioned API, keyed by Asana gid and PR, that accepts a verdict from any modality (CinC, device, curl, Playwright) only together with its evidence. (3) Asana intake through the existing V2a parser, so known behaviours and do-not-file items are pinned before testing. (4) Asana and GitHub write-back that fires from honest evidence only and works across every product repo. (5) A readiness view of sessions, fixtures and environment facts that lists the human actions blocking automation. Everything that is simulated, mock-fed, AI-gated behind an unfunded key, or has never held a single record goes. That covers the demo cockpit, mock tasks, Overview, Pipelines, Manual Test, SKB Docs, the TestCollab Plans/Runs/Requirements/Traceability/Releases/Defects/Risks modules, Performance, and the login/roles layer on a loopback-only single-user tool. It is roughly 10k LOC, and nothing the user relies on goes with it.

designs.thesis: After this pass TestPilot should be a small, honest QA backbone that Claude sessions and the user can trust, not a TestCollab-plus-cockpit demo. The load-bearing core stays and gets hardened: the Playwright/Maestro/iOS runner, the V1 verdict floor, the I1 session canary and run gate, the Scheduler monitors, and the G3 API guard (Host allowlist, Origin, nonce). Also kept: the Asana and GitHub proxies that Claude calls as an API (/api/asana/task|comment|complete-task, /api/tm/state|save, and every route the testpilot-qa skill uses), the SQLite TM database with backup-on-write, Fixtures, Run Story and run history, and TM Test Cases as the shared record of what was tested. Three things go. First, everything that fakes a result: about 750 LOC of simulated store flows, about 930 LOC of demo cards and modals, and the mock tasks, issues and notifications. One of those fakes can currently lead to a real Asana completion. Second, every surface the live data shows was never used: Plans, Runs, Requirements, Traceability, Risks, Pipelines, SKB, all with 0 rows or 0 runs, and probably Releases, Defects, Performance and the in-app AI. Third, about 2,170 LOC of seed and backfill code that has already been applied. Before deleting anything, close four risks. (1) Take a snapshot, because only 5 files are git-tracked and packages/qa-core has 0. (2) Fix the lp-shopify mapping, which today points Verify-fix at the wrong suite, so a pass there can close a GitHub issue on the wrong evidence. (3) Gate the Asana close on an honest verdict. (4) Make TM writes conflict-safe and bound the backups. The DB is 49 MB, 90% of it snapshots, and every write today replaces the whole state, so the last writer wins. Run every server-side edit outside the Sun/Wed 08:00 monitor windows and while no run is active: any server/*.ts edit restarts Vite under the LaunchAgent and kills an in-flight run, which then shows as NOT_RUN.

RUN-START DUPLICATION. 10 UIs start real runner runs: TestRunner (spec/smoke/full); TestPlans RunAutomation (TestPlans.tsx:219-381, a copy of the TestRunner picker); TaskRunnerCard (smoke/full); Pipelines; the Scheduler run-now script terminal (Schedule.tsx:100) and per-schedule Run now (:389); the Reports smoke-report builder (Reports.tsx:131) and flaky Re-run 5× (:170); ManualTest (4 call sites); TestCases runCase/runCases/runCaseOnDevice (5 sites); TestRuns runCase (:223); QaQueue Test issue/Verify fix. Suggested consolidation: one Run surface (Test Runner + its script runner), RunPanel added to TestCases, and drop RunAutomation, TaskRunnerCard, the Scheduler terminal and the Reports builder.

OVERLAPPING SCREENS. (a) Two dashboards: '/' TM Dashboard and '/overview' cockpit Overview, both with the LayoutDashboard icon; Overview is ~50% mock-driven. (b) QA Log (/qa-log, 103 LOC) is wholly duplicated by Reports section 1, 'Verified & closed'; both read useStore.qaLog. (c) 4 defect/bug models: mock Issue slice + fake fileIssue, TmDefect (0 rows), GitHub via BugsForPr/Verify fix (real), and the user's report-qa-finding skill (real). (d) Two test-case models: simulated Task.tests phases (types.ts TestCase/Phase) and real TmCase. (e) 7 AI authoring entry points (QaAuthoringCard, Hand to AI, auto-author, TM QA Copilot, TestPlans createPlanFromPr, Requirements Analyze coverage, ManualTest Ask AI/Generate spec), plus Reports flaky Diagnose and SKB, all behind the same unfunded key.

The copies: TM_FRAMEWORKS (src/tm/types.ts:341, 8 entries, missing iam-android, iam-ios and pushengage-android-sdk), FRAMEWORK_PRODUCT (src/tm/store.ts:~57), PRODUCT_FRAMEWORK (src/lib/qaPlanner.ts:35, which holds the lp-shopify bug), and the products/repos catalog in src/data/mock.ts:27-180. TM Dashboard quality-metrics row (Dashboard.tsx:60-92): 4 of the 5 tiles depend on requirements and TM defects, both 0. Real defects live on GitHub, so escape rate and defect density are permanently '—' or 0, which is misleading. Drive those tiles from GitHub issue data or drop them.

Stored-XSS sink. tm/store.ts logActivity interpolates unescaped titles into HTML: case titles from imported Playwright specs (:1419, :1769), PR titles in createPlanFromPr (:1882), suite names, defect and requirement titles. That HTML lands in the shared SQLite DB and is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML in src/screens/tm/Dashboard.tsx:216. The same pattern appears in Header.tsx:157 (notifications, including fileIssue dev names from Asana creators) and taskDetail/RightColumn.tsx:131. Low risk (loopback), but the input comes from GitHub, Asana and spec titles.

Header inconsistencies (src/components/layout/Header.tsx). The brand toggle shows on every page but only 6 automation screens read s.brand; all TM screens, Reports, Manual Test and Fixtures ignore it. The global 'Search tasks, issues…' input (:98) only filters QaQueue. CRUMBS (:11) lacks /tests/performance, /skb-docs and /runs/:id (they show 'TestPilot') and keeps the hidden /tests/risks. The bell shows only mock notifications; real session-canary or schedule changes never post one.

TM case history stores runId (src/tm/types.ts:137) but TestCases.tsx never links to /runs/:id. From a case you can't reach the Run Story (steps, screenshots, terminal) for the run that set its status, even though that is the main evidence view.

useTm.serverDown (tm/store.ts:1253) is set when the SQLite backend is unreachable, but no component reads it. The app silently falls back to localStorage-only, so edits look saved but never reach the shared DB. Surface a banner, for example in the Sidebar or Header.

Scheduled monitors give no signal: 36 of 37 test:scheduled:prod runs (pushengage-site and ledgerport-marketing-site, Sun/Wed 08:00, since 2026-08-09) FAILED; only 2026-09-16 passed. Either the suites are over-strict or the target is broken. In both cases the Scheduler's alerting is noise until it is triaged.

Auto-author defaults ON (Integrations / useStore readAutoAuthor) while /api/ai/status reports ready:true just because a key exists, and the key is unfunded. Every connector sync (~100 Asana tasks) therefore fires at least one failing AI call and a 402 toast before the burst stops. Default it off, or have /api/ai/status probe the balance.

Database screen (src/screens/Database.tsx) shows only localStorage plus the mock 'Issues' tab. It has no view of the real TM SQLite DB or its write-ahead backups, although the server already exposes /api/tm/backups and /api/tm/restore and the client has dead listTmBackups/restoreTmBackup. Repurpose it as a TM DB backup/restore console.

Seeds: 10 src/tm/*Seed.ts files (1600 LOC, 466 cases) ship in the client bundle and run 11 nested backfills (tm/store.ts:698) on every load and hydrate. With the server DB as the source of truth, they could become one-time server migrations, or be retired as CLAUDE.md plans once their Asana tasks are imported. That has never happened: 0 externalRef cases.

Unused npm dependencies: 6 of 8 @radix-ui packages (checkbox, dropdown-menu, select, slot, tabs, tooltip), class-variance-authority, and @tanstack/react-query (provider mounted in src/main.tsx with no queries). Only @radix-ui/react-dialog (Modal.tsx) and react-popover (FilterMenu.tsx) are imported.

Simulated 'Open spec folder' button (src/screens/TaskDetail.tsx:199) has no handler. SpecEditorModal (src/components/modals/SpecEditorModal.tsx:9 specSource) shows a fabricated spec template rather than the real file.

Doc drift. CLAUDE.md lists dev routes 'Overview · QA Queue · Bugs', but no Bugs route exists. CLAUDE.md says 'Accounts with no hash accept any password (demo)', but lib/users.ts verifyPassword returns false with no hash. The lib/users.ts:1-3 comment says 'no password check'. The tm/store.ts:1-5 comment says it persists to localStorage (it's SQLite now). The /skb-docs screen (604 LOC) and its sidebar entry are not documented in CLAUDE.md at all.

Overview.tsx greeting and 'came in today' are hard-coded to Asia/Kolkata (isTodayIST, line 34) instead of the browser locale. The sidebar logo (Sidebar.tsx) and Overview origin-donut colours use raw hex values, contrary to the token rule in CLAUDE.md. Minor.

Suggested keep set, based on actual use: TM Test Cases (+RunPanel), TM Dashboard (trimmed), Test Runner + Sessions, Scheduler, Reports (history, flaky, run story; absorb QA Log), Fixtures, Integrations, and a slimmed QA Queue/Task Detail limited to the real GitHub Verify-fix, Asana Close and BugsForPr. Removal candidates (roughly 9-10k LOC): the simulated task pipeline layer, mock tasks/issues/notifications, Overview, Pipelines, Manual Test (or fold its API mode into the runner), SKB Docs, TestPlans, TestRuns, Requirements, Traceability, Releases, Defects, Risks, Performance, the login/users/roles layer, and the dead exports and unused deps listed in deadCode.

server/authStore.ts (156 LOC) + api.ts authHandler/authGuard/API_ROUTE_ROLES/parseCookies/cookieAttrs (about 140 LOC): never mounted in dev (TP_AUTH unset), and no client code calls /api/auth/*.
server/index.ts (85 LOC) + package.json `start` + express/@types/express deps + dist/: not used by the LaunchAgent or any skill. With auth on by default it cannot serve the SPA.

runner.ts sessionInfo() + SessionInfo type + FrameworkHealth.session (runner.ts:357-418): no UI reads `.session`, and the src/lib/runner.ts:6 SessionInfo type is unused. Superseded by the I1 sessions.ts probes. The two disagree: /api/runner/frameworks says 'stale' for all 6 auth frameworks while the probes say warn/block.
Never-referenced exports: authStore.listUsers, authStore.pruneSessions, pipeline.activePipelineId, tmStore.hasState (each appears only at its declaration).
aiTest.ts ant-profile chain (configDir, activeProfileName, hasAntProfile, the sendMessage profile retry): cannot run here (no ~/.config/anthropic and no `ant` CLI on PATH).
Registry entry pushengage-android-sdk (runner.ts:266-283): 0 runs in the 200-entry history (2026-08-07 to 10-18). iam-android covers on-device Maestro runs.

Functionally unused, though live code: /api/pipeline/* (0 pipeline stage runs in history; in-memory list []), /api/perf/run (0 perfRuns in the TM DB), /api/devrun/* (last report 2026-08-14), POST /api/runner/adhoc (0 adhoc runs in history), /api/tm/import/asana/:gid (0 imported cases), /api/qa/export + /api/ai/save + /api/qa/cases (no .xlsx in testpilot-qa-records, no ai-generated/ dir in any framework), /api/skb/create (credentials empty).
NOT dead despite having no src caller: GET /api/schedule/alert-status and POST /api/schedule/test-alert. Both are used by ~/.claude/skills/testpilot-qa/SKILL.md:128-136.
findings: Scheduled monitors fail with nobody told. SLACK_BOT_TOKEN is declared but empty in TestPilot/.env, and ~/Library/Logs/testpilot-dev.err.log prints 'no SLACK_BOT_TOKEN set, Slack summary skipped' on every scheduled run. 38 of the 39 `test:scheduled:prod` runs in history FAILED and 0 alerts went out. scheduler.ts already has macNotify (osascript) for the canary; reuse it for run results, or set the token.

Host sleep corrupts the always-on monitors. On 2026-10-18 the ledgerport-marketing-site run took 308 min with about 298 min asleep (79 FAIL), and pushengage-site took 70 min with about 53 min asleep. com.testpilot.dev.plist has no caffeinate, and runner.ts only detects sleep after the fact (hostSleptDuring, pmset). Wrapping scheduled spawns in `caffeinate -i` would prevent it.

Schedule collision. Both Sunday jobs fire at 08:00 into a one-at-a-time runner, so pushengage-site started at 07:39Z (about 13:09 local), five hours late, behind the 308-min LedgerPort run. Stagger the jobs, e.g. 08:00 and 10:00.

Every auth-gated framework is currently gated off. The canary at 2026-10-19T18:51Z shows 9 personas: 0 ok, 4 warn, 5 block (app-dashboard:staging expired, wp-plugin:staging expired, ledgerport-saas:staging refresh-expired, ledgerport-shopify:billingpagetesting-2 expired, ledgerport-shopify:silverlisting wrong-account). Any spec/smoke/full run for those envs ends BLOCKED{SESSION} before spawning.

QA Queue GitHub feed misses most issues. GITHUB_REPO is set (awesomemotive/pushengage-sdks), so listMyIssues (server/github.ts:188-198) queries creator/assignee in that ONE repo. The user files issues across pushengage-app, omnysync, android/ios-sdk-internal, pushengage-site, etc. Unsetting GITHUB_REPO switches to the cross-repo `is:issue is:open involves:me` search, but GITHUB_REPO is also the default repo for /api/skb/analyze and /api/github/repo-issues|prs|pr.

AI surface is effectively dead weight. /api/ai/status reports ready:true/source:key because it only checks that a key exists, but the key is unfunded (memory) and there is no ant profile, so /api/ai/interpret|generate, /api/qa/plan|scenarios|cases|coverage, /api/flaky/diagnose and /api/skb/analyze|compose (AI path) all 402. No artifact exists from them: no ai-generated/ dir in any framework and no .xlsx in testpilot-qa-records. That is about 1250 server LOC (aiTest 303, qaPlanner 606, flaky diagnose, handlers), plus the auto-author pass on every connector sync in useStore.

SKB Docs is broken end to end. SKB_WP_USER and SKB_WP_APP_PASSWORD are empty, and .testpilot-skb-index.json (2026-08-26) has source 'public' with 0 articles (the public ht-kb route returns 401 per the skbDocs.ts comment; memory notes XML-RPC 403). /api/skb/create cannot work. That is 599 + 82 LOC server code plus a sidebar screen.

The TM database is dormant and mostly empty outside cases. GET /api/tm/state has 3060 cases / 172 suites, but 0 plans, executions, requirements, risks, releases, defects, perfRuns and deviceRuns. 2847 of the 3060 cases are 'unexecuted'. Only 19 writes ever (2026-08-29 to 2026-09-27), none from the UI autosave (reason 'save', src/tm/store.ts:747); all were scripted Claude backfills or hydrate-reconcile. So Plans, Runs, Requirements, Releases, Defects, Traceability and Performance have never held data in the shared DB.

Actual runner usage (200-entry history, 2026-08-07 to 10-18): pushengage-wp-plugin 64, pushengage-site 48, iam-android 33, ledgerport-marketing-site 25, pushengage-app-dashboard 18, iam-ios 11, ledgerport-shopify 1. pushengage-shopify-revamped, ledgerport-saas-automation, ledgerport-wp-plugin and pushengage-android-sdk have 0. By mode: spec 110, command 41 (all test:scheduled:prod or test:smoke:report:prod), maestro 33, ios 11, full 3, smoke 2, adhoc 0, pipeline 0. Since 2026-09-01 the only runs are the scheduled monitors plus a few testpilot-qa skill runs.

Second, competing scheduler. ~/QA-Automations/smoke-monitor runs com.awesomemotive.qa.smoke-all and com.awesomemotive.qa.smoke-auth-ctas via launchd directly against the same frameworks, bypassing TestPilot (no verdict floor, no session gate). Its last report (2026-10-19) was 0 passed / 7 failed. Consolidate into TestPilot schedules, or retire one.

Production-hosting path is half-built. server/index.ts mounts auth by default (TP_AUTH!=='0'), but the SPA never calls /api/auth/login (no /api/auth or credentials:'include' in src/), so `npm start` would 401 every API call. Also, authStore.pruneSessions is never called, and the SEED_USERS list with the admin passwordHash literal is duplicated in server/authStore.ts:37 and src/lib/users.ts. Memory says the mirror repo is public.

server/api.ts duplication. All 19 handler factories repeat res.setHeader('Content-Type')/send()/isSameOrigin()/JSON.parse(await readBody(...)). Malformed JSON surfaces as 500 rather than 400 everywhere except sessionsHandler, and perfHandler maps every error to 400. A small route table (method, path regex, body limit, needsNonce, handler) could remove about 200 LOC and make the role map (API_ROUTE_ROLES) and nonce list declarative.
api.ts:803 hard-codes model 'claude-opus-4-8' in /api/ai/status instead of importing MODEL from aiTest.ts:20, so the two can drift.

GET routes with process or network side effects need no Origin, so a cross-site page can trigger them with a plain GET (the Host allowlist only stops DNS rebinding). /api/runner/specs?refresh=1 spawns `playwright test --list` for up to 120 s (runner.ts:491); /api/sessions without cached=1 spawns `npm run auth:probe` per stale persona (sessions.ts:233); /api/skb/index?refresh=1 makes external fetches. Low severity on loopback; a Sec-Fetch-Site check like the nonce route's would close it.
/api/perf/run (server/perf.ts:76) sends real load (up to 50 VUs x 120 s x 10 targets) to any URL without the qa-core assertAllowedTarget guard that ad-hoc runs use, so it can load-test production.

Mobile harness defaults are hard-coded in runner.ts: the maestro APP_ID default 3ca8257d… and the ios APP_ID default 3bd8264e…. They belong in the D4 fixture registry (config/fixtures.json), not in code.

The registry contradicts itself about the Android toolchain. The pushengage-android-sdk notes say JDK17/Android SDK/maestro are not on the host, while the iam-android notes say the host has them; the first has 0 runs. The LaunchAgent PATH also omits /opt/homebrew/bin, so mobile runs depend on run.sh/env.sh sourcing their own PATH.
Pipelines are memory-only (pipeline.ts Map). Any Vite restart, including every server/*.ts edit, erases them; they were never used in the retained history.

Naming trap: useStore.ts:1791 postAsanaComment is a SIMULATED Demo comment, while src/lib/asana.ts:43 postAsanaComment is the real write and is never imported. The real /api/asana/comment route has no UI caller.

Version-control risk before any removal. In the QA-Automations repo, git status shows server/api.ts, every other server/*.ts, server/qaLoop/, vite.config.ts and package.json as untracked (??); only server/runner.ts is tracked (modified). Snapshot or commit (e.g. to the KulvinderGosal/TestPilot mirror) before deleting or refactoring.

Connector health (GET only): Asana connected:true, GitHub connected:true, Slack no_token. ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID is empty (auto-picks a workspace). TP_ALLOWED_HOSTS, QA_FIXTURES_PATH, TP_SESSION_CANARY, TP_CANARY_NOTIFY, TP_AUTH, QA_ROOT and PORT are not set in .env, so all take their defaults.

Every route the testpilot-qa skill calls must keep its contract through any refactor: GET /api/runner/frameworks, POST /api/runner/runs, GET /api/runner/runs/:id, GET /api/reports/history, GET /api/sessions, and /api/schedule list/alert-status/test-alert/create/:id/run/:id/toggle. /api/tm/state + /api/tm/save are also used by Claude backfill sessions.

findings: HIGH (honesty / real write): the simulated flows can produce the only gate for a REAL Asana write. TaskDetail.tsx:89-93 shows 'Close task' when task.status==='verified'. Simulated runTestPlan in 'verify' mode sets that status (useStore.ts:931), and so does runQaPipeline's scripted arc (useStore.ts:1886-2002: forced failure, fake issue, fake dev fix, verify). closeTask (useStore.ts:1059-1115) then calls completeAsanaTask, which does PUT completed:true, and writes a durable qaLog entry. On a real Asana task this is reachable as 'Generate from task' → 'Run QA pipeline' → 'Close task' with no runner run at all. This contradicts the V1 floor that verifyGithubFix enforces (isHonestPass). Gate closeTask on an honest runner verdict or an explicit manual sign-off, or delete the simulated paths.

HIGH (mock data in a live queue): mock fixtures never fully leave the queue. loadAsana/loadGithub/loadSlack each replace only their own origin (useStore.ts:1245/1297/1353), so the 6 origin-'manual' mock tasks (task-2/3/5/6/9/10, mock.ts:236-332) can never be replaced. Slack is not configured (live GET /api/slack/tasks → connected:false, reason:no_token), so task-7 and task-11 stay as well: 8 of 11 mock tasks are permanently shown in QA Queue, Overview, Database and the Sidebar badge. The badge is inflated by 4 (Sidebar.tsx:55-57). task-10 shows 'running 15%' forever (mock.ts:715). task-5 and task-6 start 'verified', so 'Close task' on a fictional task writes a durable QA Log entry. MEDIUM (dead seed weight): every TM seed backfill is a no-op today (live seq at current versions, all 466 seed cases in the DB). Still, 10 seed files (~1,600 LOC, ~193 KB) plus ~570 lines of build/backfill/seed code in tm/store.ts ship in the single 1.07 MB bundle and run 11 guard checks on every hydrate. Safe removal path: (1) keep IAM_IOS_ASSERT next to assessIosRun; (2) reduce seed() to the 10 product suites, or seed fresh installs from a DB export or backup; (3) delete *Seed.ts and the backfills. Recording new session results should go through the V2a Asana import or a TM write API, not new seed files. The three newer seed guards (iamCollateralSeed, lpIssue19Seed, onb1015Seed) already exist only as DB data.

MEDIUM (duplication): 7 of the 11 backfill functions are near-identical ~22-line bodies (tm/store.ts:170-191, 425-446, 453-471, 474-492, 495-513, 520-538, 544-562), differing only in seq key, suites, cases and label. They are composed as an 11-deep nested call (store.ts:698). Each new seed has cost about 25 LOC of boilerplate plus an import plus a version constant.

MEDIUM (efficiency/data risk): the TM state is a 2,416,923-char JSON blob (3,060 cases, 2,494 of them imp-). Every TM mutation calls after() → persist(), which synchronously JSON.stringifies the whole blob into localStorage (store.ts:755-761) and POSTs it in full (store.ts:739-752). createPlanFromPr calls addCase up to 19 times (store.ts:1843-1915), giving 19+ full serializations; bulk runs persist once per case. About 2.4M chars is roughly 4.8 MB as UTF-16, right at the usual ~5 MB localStorage quota, and save() swallows QuotaExceededError silently, so the mirror can go stale. Move to per-entity/patch writes, or drop the full mirror.

MEDIUM (data integrity): hydrate decides between local and server by case COUNT: `localOk && local.cases.length > srvBase.cases.length ? local : server` (store.ts:1271). A stale mirror with more cases resurrects cases deleted elsewhere, and a local deletion that never reached the server is silently undone. Compare an updatedAt/version stamp instead.

GET /api/tm/state shows plans 0, executions 0, requirements 0, risks 0, releases 0, defects 0, perfRuns 0, deviceRuns 0. That covers TestPlans 591 + TestRuns 244 + Requirements 414 + Traceability 231 + Releases 415 + Defects 341 + Performance 366 + Risks 374 = 2,976 screen LOC, plus about 330 store LOC (store.ts:1801-2115). Playwright suites/scripts run directly in the framework dir or a workflow (AI generator, 7-day trial, pricing #465, Silver Listing marketing spec) about 15%. API/curl as the primary oracle about 10%, but used as supporting evidence in roughly 40% (always with a browser UA for Cloudflare). Code/bundle/gh inspection as corroboration in about 30% (the user insists it never replaces the UI). TestPilot runner 0-4% (one real use, the 10-12 silver-listing verdict demo). Scheduled monitors are background only: 29 runs since 09-01, 28 red. User-performed steps appear in at least 10 of the ~13 auth-gated web engagements: password/Turnstile/OTP/2FA/passkey, Shopify 'Approve' charge, plan upgrade clicks, typing a 36-char App ID into the emulator, DevTools device mode for real 375px, Safari/Firefox runs, loading staging once for cf_clearance, placing storefront orders, downloading APKs, buying AI credits.

(c) PAIN POINT: AUTH DECAY IS THE NUMBER ONE BLOCKER. JWTs last 15 min, storageState about 7 days, and the gates are Turnstile, hCaptcha (broken by trace/video), Shopify passkeys, mandatory 2FA and email OTP. Personas right now: 0 ok, 4 warn, 5 block. On Silver Listing the user pasted JWTs. The always-valid authenticated surface is the user's Chrome, but the rule 'never bridge the logged-in Chrome token into Playwright' keeps the runner off it. Only app-dashboard has the auth:capture:human (log in in normal Chrome, then read via CDP) path.

(c) PAIN POINT: AUTOMATION-HOSTILE SURFACES. Cloudflare WAF blocks automated browsers on the staging dashboard, qaprod (manual challenge) and api-staging (needs a browser UA), and rate-limits marketing crawls. Cross-origin Shopify iframes can't be driven by CinC. navigator.webdriver=true makes the PushEngage SDK report push unsupported in any Playwright browser. Shopify rejects Playwright's iPad/iPhone UAs. CinC limits: resize_window doesn't change innerWidth, read_network_requests misses XHRs, output containing URLs or tokens gets stripped, and Chrome autofill and 1Password interfere. Intuit My Apps and the consent popup are unreachable.

(c) PAIN POINT: TEST DATA AND ORACLES OWNED BY OTHERS. Missing plan-variant accounts and stores (Free/Growth/Enterprise, 0-credit vs funded AI credits, single-step-drip, no-multi-action, unverified-email, 2FA-off). Shopify dev-store order caps. A shared QB realm makes SL-T1-01 untestable alone. Some oracles only devs can read: server logs and the DB (5 SL-T cases), Redis and token replay (refresh tokens), cron fan-out (subscriber timezone). Purchases and approvals are blocked by the safety classifier. The consequences: one false PASS by inference (SL-T1-01, reopened by the dev) and two false positives from screenshots without logs or PR scope (ios #58, #59).

(c) PAIN POINT: DEPLOY UNCERTAINTY AND HOST/TOOLING FRAGILITY. 'Is the fix on staging?' gets answered by grepping the bundle (onboarding #1015 chunk 42.aeb710fd). Staging runs feature branches, so 'not on master' does not mean 'not deployed'. Prod is cached by Cloudflare APO. The host is a MacBook Air that sleeps (an 18.4 h run was asleep 16.8 h). Playwright Firefox won't launch on macOS 27. The Xcode license breaks git and python3. On mobile: emulator ANRs and GPU flags, Maestro IME doubling the first character, simulator rotation blocked by the Accessibility permission, iOS builds that are TestFlight-only, APKs that can't be fetched from Asana. Suite-quality debt: ledgerport-shopify never asserted QB outcomes; requireAppOrSkip gave a 2 s false skip; 596 Excel stub files; stale selectors in 0306/0307. The user also wants speed and terse output ('moving like a junior tester').

(d) WHY TESTPILOT IS BYPASSED AT EACH STEP. INTAKE: the queue is truncated to 100 (server/asana.ts:158) and is 85% case-subtask noise; GitHub sees one of about 8 repos; Slack has no token, so mock tasks remain. Pasting a gid into chat plus the Asana MCP is faster, and V2a import has 0 uses. PLANNING: plans have to be shareable with devs and the PR author, but TestPilot is loopback-only, so they live in claude.ai artifacts and the test-plan-generator output (TM plans: 0). EXECUTION: auth personas are dead, so the runner can't reach logged-in surfaces; the live session is in the user's Chrome. The runner's envOptions don't model ad-hoc store, handle and account overrides. It runs one job at a time and can't host a parallel Playwright workflow. Device modes only cover the fire-event/launch subset. RECORDING: every engagement needed a new seed .ts file plus a store.ts backfill, so it was abandoned after 09-27. REPORT/CLOSE: gh with /report-qa-finding is already precise; TestPilot's fileIssue is fake and verify-fix is single-repo and whole-smoke. MONITORING: it runs but nobody acts on it, because it is always red, sleep-corrupted and has no Slack.

(d) WHERE TESTPILOT IS ACTUALLY USED. (1) The scheduler and canary run unattended. (2) The honest verdict floor and host-sleep logic are relied on by run-product.sh. (3) The Asana/GitHub proxy has been used as an API by Claude (heavily in Aug-Sep; G3's X-TP-Nonce on /api/asana/comment and complete-task now makes curl use awkward). (4) The runner, in August bursts: wp-plugin 63 spec runs, pushengage-site 25, app-dashboard 18, IAM device 44. (5) TM as a read-only 'record of what was tested' via seeds until 09-27.

(e) WHAT TESTPILOT SHOULD BE, PART 1: a QA-engagement ledger that Claude writes to over an API, keyed by Asana gid and PR. One row per engagement holds product x surface, env, PRs, deploy status and the dev's known-behaviours/do-not-file list. Each case carries a verdict from any modality (CinC, curl, adb, simctl, Playwright) with evidence pointers: screenshot path, log excerpt such as logcat or --console-pty display records, API response, and the issue URL. PASS is allowed only with an oracle recorded; otherwise UNVERIFIED with the need stated. The pieces already exist: the V2a intake parser (809 lines, extracts Steps/Pass/Fail/Known behaviours), TmCase.externalRef and the verdict states. What changes is that results are written as data through POST /api/tm/... rather than as seed .ts files, and write-back comes from the ledger: a short Asana comment plus complete, and gh close across every repo (search with involves:viewer, or a GITHUB_REPOS list).

(e) PART 2: an auth and environment readiness hub. Per engagement it would show which personas, accounts and fixtures are needed and which are dead, with one daily 'human actions' list (exact capture commands, CF clearance, accounts to create). The auth:capture:human pattern (user logs in in normal Chrome, CDP reads the session) would be extended to every framework. Env facts that now live in memory would move into config/fixtures.json: site 51041, QA-Android-iOS-apps 3bd8264e, prod ffedc363/76524, stores, QB realms, plan-variant and credit accounts. A deploy-presence check ('is PR X live on staging?', by bundle-grep or commit marker per env) would be added.

(e) PART 3: one trustworthy monitor instead of three. Keep TestPilot's Scheduler and retire the launchd smoke-all and smoke-auth-ctas, or the reverse. Pin to chromium, skip when the lid is closed or wrap in caffeinate, and quarantine known-red and staging-only tests so 'green when healthy' holds. Either wire SLACK_BOT_TOKEN or rely on the macOS notification. Run auth-gated legs only when their persona is ok. Mobile: either make iam-android/iam-ios runner entries match how mobile QA is actually run (env.sh, run-case.sh, adb broadcast FIRE_IAM, simctl defaults writes, log capture as the oracle) or drop them.

(e) FEATURES THAT DON'T FIT THIS PROCESS (removal candidates, with evidence). TM Requirements + AI coverage gap, Traceability, Releases GO/NO-GO, Defects, Risks and Performance: all seq counters are 0, about 3,100 lines including perf.ts. TM Test Plans/Test Runs/PR-to-plan: 0 plans and 0 executions. TM Dashboard quality metrics: derived from empty slices. All in-app AI (QA Copilot, AI QA authoring + auto-author, Ask AI, flaky Diagnose, SKB compose; about 1,800 server lines): 402 since July, and Claude Code does this work. SKB Docs: skbReady false, XML-RPC 403. Pipelines and Manual Test ad-hoc: 0 runs since 08-07. The simulated cockpit (runTestPlan, simulateDevFix, fileIssue, mergeTask, DemoBadge flows, mock tasks/issues from src/data/mock.ts; TaskDetail tree 1,771 lines). The Overview donuts, computed over the mock-polluted queue. The 2,494 imp- cases (1.5% ever executed, many tied to stub specs now ignored), which should be pruned to the curated @case-bound ones. The 10 seed files. Login/Users/Database multi-role: park unless the VPS hosting plan resumes.

(e) KEEP AND HARDEN: runner + V1 verdict floor + host-sleep detection; I1 session canary and run gate (add recovery actions); the Asana/GitHub read/write proxy (multi-repo, remove the 100 cap, filter case subtasks out of the queue and group them under their parent); V2a intake parser plus @case binding; Fixtures registry; Run Story and run history; the testpilot-qa skill. Watch for friction: the G3 nonce on write routes means Claude's own curl write-backs need GET /api/session/nonce first, so if the ledger becomes Claude's API surface, plan a scripted nonce flow or a local CLI.

KEY NUMBERS FOR THE NEXT PHASE: 34,556 lines in src+server. TM 3,060 cases (2,847 unexecuted), DB last write 09-27, 49 MB plus a 13.6 MB WAL. Run history: 200 entries, 122 failed, 75 passed, 3 blocked; Sep-Oct = 33 runs, 29 of them scheduled. Asana queue: 100 items (cap), 85 case subtasks, 68 IAM-*. Personas: 0/9 ok. findings: BUG (data loss, CONFIRMED by code path) src/tm/store.ts:1252-1253 + :925. If GET /api/tm/state fails during hydrate (e.g. the LaunchAgent's Vite restart after any server/*.ts edit), the store loads the localStorage mirror with hydrated:true/serverDown:true. Every later mutation then calls pushToServer, so when the server comes back the stale mirror overwrites the whole server DB blob (saveState has no version check). Edits made by Claude sessions or other tabs in between are silently replaced; they are recoverable only via /api/tm/backups, which has no UI.

BUG (lost writes, CONFIRMED) src/tm/store.ts:738-752 + server/tmStore.ts:125-170. Every client mutation POSTs the ENTIRE 2.4MB state as last-writer-wins, with no etag/updated_at precondition. A tab that hydrated before a Claude session's /api/tm/save (backups show reasons such as 'pre:ONB-AI-05 executed live on qastaging') overwrites those server-side updates on its next click. Only the Asana import path merges server writes (applyAsanaImport). The >90%-drop warning (tmStore.ts:162) does not catch same-count overwrites.

BUG (PLAUSIBLE) src/tm/store.ts:1271. The hydrate heuristic prefers the localStorage mirror whenever it has MORE cases than the server, then pushes it as 'hydrate-reconcile'.
